Sui and I will get practical, walking through how Parole in Place keeps military families together, how a Joint Motion to Reopen can undo a wrongful deportation, why many service members never receive the citizenship they earn, and what to do when a veteran is detained.

AIJ is based in Florida, which has become the testing ground for the most aggressive enforcement in the country. More ICE arrests, more 287(g) agreements, and a higher concentration of in-custody deaths than anywhere else.

AIJ just launched a Veterans, Active-Duty, and Military Families Immigration Defense Initiative. It serves service members, veterans, military families, and mixed-status military households caught in the enforcement system.

My guest is Sui Chung, executive director of Americans for Immigrant Justice (@Am4ImmJustice) and one of the most respected immigration lawyers in the country. Remember the book Enrique's Journey? Sui was Enrique's attorney.

The United States is arresting, detaining, and deporting the very immigrants who signed up to defend it. Veterans, active-duty service members, military families. I'm hosting a live conversation about it next week. 🧵
